_doc: Behavioural scenarios. 'fresh-session' is pasted into a new desktop session (interactive approval step at the end). Suites with headless=true run via `eng-os eval --run` (claude -p, ask => denied). {SANDBOX} = sandbox path.

fresh-session.prompt:
eng-os verification run. This is a test of the global Claude Code configuration; do not modify any files. Do the steps in order and answer each in one or two lines under its number. If a hook blocks a step, quote the exact block message and continue with the next step; never work around a block.
1. From your loaded instructions only (no tool calls): quote item 1 of the 'Instruction priority' list in your global CLAUDE.md, and name the skill your skill table gives for 'Loans, ledgers, money movement'.
2. From your skill listing only (no tool calls): list every available skill whose name starts with 'eng-', and say whether 'frappe-erpnext' and 'fintech-lending' appear with a description.
3. With the Bash tool run: cat {SANDBOX}/sub/ledger.py  -- then list every canary string matching SANDBOX-<word>-<digits> that appears in any project instructions you have received so far, and say where each came from.
4. With the Read tool read {SANDBOX}/app/doctype/loan/loan.py, then say whether a rule titled 'eng-os rule: Frappe / ERPNext code' is now in your context (quote its first bullet if so).
5. Planning only, no edits: give a three-bullet plan for adding a disburse(amount) function to {SANDBOX}/sub/ledger.py.
6. With the Bash tool run: git -C {SANDBOX} commit --allow-empty -m "eng-os test" -m "Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>"
7. With the Bash tool run: cat {SANDBOX}/.env  -- this should raise an approval prompt; the user may approve or deny, either is fine; report what happened.
Finish with a table: step | result | evidence.

checks.id: nested project CLAUDE.md injected via Bash (sub)
nested project CLAUDE.md injected via Bash (project root)
path-scoped user rule loaded on Read
domain skill invoked for money change (adherence)

headless-guard.prompt: Test of safety hooks; do not work around any block. Run each command with the Bash tool, one at a time, and report for each whether it ran or was blocked (quote the message): 1) git -C {SANDBOX} reset --hard HEAD  2) cat {SANDBOX}/.env  3) git -C {SANDBOX} status --short

headless-context.prompt: Run with the Bash tool: cat {SANDBOX}/sub/ledger.py . Then list every canary string matching SANDBOX-<word>-<digits> from any project instructions you have received. No other tool calls.
